blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Part III of the Indian Constitution contains six Fundamental Rights covering Articles 12 to 35, which are justiciable in nature.
Article 32 guarantees the Right to Constitutional Remedies, provides five types of writs, and is considered the 'Heart and Soul of Constitution'.
Key individual rights include Article 17 (Abolition of Untouchability), Article 21 (Protection of life and liberty), and Article 21A (Right to Education).
Directive Principles of State Policy are placed in Part IV (Articles 36 to 51), whereas Fundamental Duties are in Part IVA (Article 51A).
Article 32 is frequently tested as the 'Heart and Soul of Constitution' and the source for five types of writs.
Judicial Review specifically originates from Article 13.
Right to Property is classified as a Legal Right rather than a Fundamental Right.
Do not confuse the parts: Part III (Fundamental Rights), Part IV (DPSP), and Part IVA (Fundamental Duties).
